tracks.narration: An op-amp with no feedback resistor — how does it turn a smooth voltage into a clean digital decision?
V in goes to the plus input, a fixed reference V ref to the minus input. There is no feedback wire — the op-amp runs open loop, with a gain in the hundreds of thousands.
The transfer characteristic is brutal. Below V ref the output sits at minus V sat. Above V ref it jumps to plus V sat. The transition is essentially vertical.
Feed it a triangle wave. Each time the input climbs past V ref, the output snaps high; each time it falls back below, the output snaps low. A smooth analog input becomes a clean square wave.
That is what a comparator does — turn an analog crossing into a digital edge. Zero-crossing detectors, level alarms, every analog-to-digital converter starts here.
